newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Ege Profil aims to raise exports.
newsitem.headline: Turk Ege Profil aims to raise exports.

text.p: Turkey's plastic profiles and granules producer Ege Profil Ticaret ve Sanayi A.S. exceeded its growth target and increased export sales in the first half of the year, a company official said on Monday.
The company reported a 290 billion lira net profit in the first half of the year, against 132 billion lira in the same period of last year.
The share of exports in total sales to rose to 11.8 percent from 1.38 percent in the period.
"High first half results show that we will exceed the 15 percent real growth target in 1997," Kemal Zorlu, deputy president of the company, told Reuters.
Total sales of the company increased by 149.6 percent to 1.98 trillion lira in the first half, from 794 billion lira in the same period of last year.
The company exceeded its 1.91 trillion lira 1996 sales in the first half of 1997.
Turkey's year-on-year consumer price inflation was 78 percent in June.
Shares of the company on the Istanbul Stock Exchange opened at lost 500 lire on Monday, closing at 10,000 lira.
Exports of Ege Profil leapt by 1,127 percent to 234 billion lira in the first half of 1997, from 11 billion lira in the same period last year.
The main export markets of the company are Germany, Israel, Cyprus, Turkmenistan, Russia and Khazakstan.
"We had a big jump in exports this year, because of the soaring demand in Eastern and Central Asian countries," Zorlu said.
"The demand for doors and windows made of plastic profiles in these countries is increasing rapidly," he added.
He said their aim was to further increase the share of the exports in total sales.
The company expanded its annual production capacity to 11,100 tonnes at the end of last year, from 8,000 tonnes the year before. Capacity utilisation of the company was 97 percent last year.
"But we will continue to spend on new technology and modernisation investments," he added.
The company began producing plastic fittings in the second half of last year and plans to expand their product range of plastic fittings this year. OSS JON
